1.14 Troubleshooting

Symptom Cause and fix
Run diskproxy-server. The camera card is not registered; see Registering a new card
A managed session already exists. A view is already running; use diskproxy status or diskproxy stop
Detach failed. Server left running... An application still has files open; close them and run diskproxy stop again
Mounted volume identity changed. Server left running. The mounted disk is not the one diskproxy attached; check it before doing anything else
Server did not provide a disk URL within 15 minutes. The scan did not finish; the server’s errors are printed above the message
A read fails with an I/O error A source or preview file changed while served; stop and start again
Ratings harvest still running ... The final capture took over two minutes; check the harvester log in the session folder and retry
Ratings check failed; disk left mounted. The replacement walk failed; see the harvester log, fix the cause and retry
Mount point ... is not empty. NFS mode mounts only on an empty folder; empty it or set mountpoint
A DNG shows only a small thumbnail Its map entry is missing, or its preview could not be composed; the server log has a warning

1.14.1 The NFS unmount hang

During early development on macOS 26, unmounting an NFS view hung inside the kernel’s NFS client three times, for between one minute and about half an hour. The volume disappeared at once, but the unmounting process sat in an uninterruptible wait with no NFS traffic, and later NFS mounts queued behind it. Since then the current server has passed 142 consecutive mount/write/unmount cycles without a hang. They were 82 direct cycles, covering both unmount methods, delayed and immediate unmounts and temporary-file-and-rename rewrites, plus 60 cycles through diskproxy start and stop. Unmounts took about 0.1 seconds and the slowest stop took 4.6 seconds. The earlier hangs may have come from the first server version and a kernel client it left degraded; the cause is not proven.

If it happens:

  • leave the stuck process alone; it clears on its own, and killing it does not help;
  • don’t start another NFS view until it clears, because new mounts queue behind it;
  • use a shadow-file view in the meantime; it does not use NFS.

The launcher unmounts with the unmount(2) system call, through diskproxy-server unmount [--force] PATH. Avoid umount and diskutil unmount for NFS views: they wait minutes afterwards for an rpcbind registration this server does not make.
